paragraphs.text: In Shanghai, sure.
Qing Song, yui, means or sicha.
Te du shamborti.
The Count of Monte Cristo.
Chapter 1.
A joyous homecoming.
One day in February 1810,
the ship Pharaoh came into the French port of Marseilles.
A man watched it from the harbor.
When he saw the Pharaoh, he got into a small boat and went out to it.
A young, handsome man stood waiting on the Pharaoh.
The older man in the small boat called out to the young man.
Is it you, Dantes?
What happened to the captain?
A very sad thing, Mr. Morel.
Answer the young man.
When our ship was near Cevitavica, we lost brave captain the Claire.
The cargo. Is the cargo safe?
Ask the older man.
Yes, Mr. Morel. The cargo is safe.
Replied the young man, then he suddenly turned and gave some orders to the men in his crew.
The crew obeyed quickly and well.
But the poor captain?
Said Dantes.
Yes, yes, tell me about the captain.
Said Morel.
Did he fall overboard?
No, sir. He died of a fever a few days after we left Naples.
Dantes said as his eyes watched the crew.
Now, please excuse me, sir. I have to help the men with the ship.
Please come on board with donglers. The business manager will explain the cargo and profit.
Morel looked at Dantes and his smile got bigger. Dantes, though young, was doing a fine job running the ship.
Morel began to think that maybe he had already found a captain to replace the dead Le Claire.
He watched Dantes a little longer. Then came on board the pharaoh. Danglers helped him onto the larger ship.
Danglers was a few years older than Dantes. No one on the ship liked Danglers.
Welcome back to your ship, Mr. Morel.
Danglers said with a smile.
I think you will find our business was very good.
Yes, Danglers. I heard from Dantes. The trip went well, except for the poor captain.
Morel answered. His eyes still watching Dantes.
Yes, the loss of the captain was terrible.
Answer Danglers.
He was a fine captain for you and your company.
Yes, but it appears young Dantes is doing well.
Said Morel.
Maybe a young man can also make a good captain.
Danglers did not like young Dantes.
Yes, but a young captain can make mistakes. Because of Dantes, we are late getting home.
Danglers said with an evil look on his face.
After the captain died, we didn't come straight to Marseilles.
Instead, we went to the island of Elba for a couple of days.
The happy look on Morel's face suddenly changed.
Why did you stop at Elba? Was there a problem with the boat?
No, nothing was wrong. We just stopped and did nothing.
Answer the clever Danglers. Morel left Danglers and called to Dantes.
Dantes, come here. I need to talk to you.
Dantes came up to Morel.
What is it, sir? Why did you stop at Elba?
Morel asked. It was the captain's last order.
Dantes answered. He told me before he died to take a letter to someone on the island.
Morel got a worried look on his face. He pulled Dantes closer and spoke softly, so no one could hear.
Did you meet Napoleon? Did you talk to him? You know this could be very dangerous.
He talked to me. I did not talk to him. Dantes answered.
Now I need to deliver a letter to Paris. What does the letter say?
Morel asked. I do not know. Dantes answered. I didn't read it. I will just take it to Paris if you give me the time.
Alright Dantes, but tell no one about the letter. It could be dangerous if the king or his men learn of it.
Understand? Morel said this quietly, looking around to see if anyone was listening. Danglers was watching, but was too far away to hear anything.
Yes, Mr. Morel. Dantes answered. Morel looked at Dantes carefully.
You are young, but wise. Dantes, are you busy? Have dinner with me.
I am sorry, sir, but it has been too long since I saw my father. After meeting my father, there is one other I have to see.
Dantes answered. Ah, yes. The beautiful Mercedes. I understand.
Morel said with a smile. Could I have some time off?
Ask Dantes. To go to Paris to deliver the letter?
Morel asked. Yes, but also to get married. Dantes answered.
Mercedes has promised to marry me. Congratulations, Dantes. Of course you can have some time off. But hurry back. A ship should not be long without her captain.
Morel said with a smile. Really, Mr. Morel? Me? Captain of the Pharaoh? Dantes was very happy.
Yes, Dantes. Now visit your father, see Mercedes, and then come to have dinner with me.
Morel said. As Dantes left the ship, Dantes watched him walk away.
He heard the last part of the conversation, the part about Dantes being the new captain of the Pharaoh.
The look on Danglers face was different from Dantes and Morel's expressions. He did not look happy.
